To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression and activity of cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzymes in human brain cells are induced by the known CYP regulators and neurotoxicant monocrotophos.
the expression and activity of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes are induced in pre-sensitised human brain cells by the organophosphorous insecticide monocrotophos.
MCP induces CYP1A, 2B and 2E in human brain cells and pre-exposure to CYP inducer increases the induction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of xenobiotic metabolizers in human brain cells by MCP and its pre-sensitizing effect on the CYPs.
the expression and metabolic profile CYPs in the human brain cells and the effect of pre-exposure to classical inducers on MCP induced CYP expression.
the expression and activity of the CYPs in human neuronal and glial cell lines, which are known to be involved in the metabolism of the xenobiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is a metabolically competent organ and is not just a passive recipient of xenobiotics.
the brain is a xenobiotic metabolically competent organ. © Springer Science+Business Media New York 2013.
MCP induces the expression of CYP1As, CYP2B6 and CYP2E1 in pre-sensitized neuronal and glial brain cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the induction of CYP1, 2 and 3 family of enzymes in the brain cells is a common phenomenon in response to a variety of xenobiotic exposure.
, the human neuronal and glial cell lines are capable of metabolizing xenobiotics, including MCP and other CYP inducers, which are known to induce CYPs in other tissues.
the human brain cells have a potential to respond to the xenobiotics, which is evident from their ability to induce the expression and activity of xenobiotic metabolizers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain cells can be used as an alternative to the brain tissue for the study of CYP expression and metabolism in brain.
the brain cells are not devoid of xenobiotic metabolising machinery and can be used as a model to study the effect of xenobiotics on brain physiology.
the human brain cells can express CYPs in response to the xenobiotic stimuli and the induction is significantly high in pre-sensitized cells.
